name: Changelog and Release Notes
description: On demand, reconcile this project's changelog with its git history, then draft a release announcement from it: the analyst reads the existing changelog and the commits in the configured range and writes a sourced analysis (what is missing, inaccurate, mis-categorized, mis-ordered, or correctly excluded); the curator edits the changelog file IN PLACE to add, correct, move, merge, and reorder entries so every one traces to a commit; the auditor re-derives the commit list from git and gates on accuracy, format, and style with a SHIP/FIX/BLOCK verdict and a bounded FIX loop; on a final SHIP the announcer reads the curated changelog and drafts a human summary plus a release announcement in the project's voice (drafts only, never posted). On a final SHIP the edited changelog auto-merges back, bounded by writeScope to changelog files only; a FIX/BLOCK run discards the edit and keeps only the run record. All project specifics (which file, its format, the range, what counts as user-facing, and the release-announcement voice and channel) come from this project's pack under .glissa/teams/changelog/pack/.

stages.summary: Reads the existing changelog and the commits in the configured range, maps every commit to its changelog state (missing / inaccurate / mis-categorized / mis-ordered / correctly excluded), and writes analysis.md with sourced proposed edits. Halts CHANGELOG_ACCURATE when the changelog already reflects the history.

Applies the analyst's proposed changes by editing the changelog file IN PLACE (within writeScope): adds missing entries, rewords inaccurate ones, moves mis-placed entries, merges duplicates, and fixes ordering; every edit traces to a commit in the analysis. Writes revision.md (the handoff summary, not the changelog).

Re-derives the commit list from read-only git and grades the edited changelog on accuracy (every entry traces to a commit and every user-facing commit is represented), format, and style; writes review.md ending in a SHIP/FIX/BLOCK verdict.

On a final SHIP, reads the curated changelog and writes published.md: a short human-facing summary of what the run reconciled (for a pull request or commit body) plus a release announcement draft in the project's voice. Drafts only; never posts, tags, or cuts a release.
